claim_text: Starbucks said it had 'an issue with Mobile Order & Pay' and apologized
summary: KTEN reports that Starbucks apologized and acknowledged 'an issue with Mobile Order & Pay' in a statement on its website.
detail: We did not read Starbucks' own statement; KTEN and a republisher of its story relay it. An earlier IBTimes Australia report said Starbucks had not yet confirmed a problem, which was probably written before the statement. It stays Reported until Starbucks' own page is read or a second outlet quotes it.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: KTEN quotes the acknowledgement and says it was in a statement on Starbucks' website; the second source is a republication of the same story, so it counts once.

claim_text: Starbucks customers had errors, zero balances and failed payments in Mobile Order & Pay on Friday, Nov 20
summary: Customers in the US saw error messages, zero balances and payment failures in the Starbucks app on Friday, Nov 20.
detail: KTEN reported error messages and zero balances. IBTimes Australia cited Downdetector for a wave of reports, mostly about the app and sign-in. The Instatus tracker shows a spike and user comments about failed payments.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: A news outlet, a second outlet citing an outage tracker, and the tracker itself describe the same symptoms independently of each other.

claim_text: Reports started rising about 10 AM ET and were back near normal about 4 PM ET
summary: The Instatus tracker shows reports rising from 3 PM UTC (10 AM ET) and back to normal at 9 PM UTC (4 PM ET), about 6 hours later.
detail: This is one automated tracker built from user reports, so times are approximate. Starbucks has not published a start or end time. On Nov 20 the tracker gave an end of 8 PM UTC (about 5 hours); by Nov 25 it had revised this to 9 PM UTC (6 hours).
label: Reported
why_it_supports: The tracker's outage page gives the 3 PM to 9 PM UTC window and its status page says reports are at their usual level.

claim_text: The tracker peaked at about 73 times its normal report rate
summary: Instatus recorded a peak of 4,586 reports an hour, about 73 times normal.
detail: Reports are not a count of affected customers or orders. The tracker revised its figure as reports came in: 2,902 an hour (50 times normal), then 3,451 an hour (58 times) on Nov 20, and 4,586 an hour (73 times) when read on Nov 25.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: The outage page states the peak rate and the multiple of normal.

claim_text: Stores and drive-thrus stayed open, and refunds for the problem were temporarily unavailable
summary: A summary of the KTEN story says customers could still order in stores and drive-thrus, and that refunds tied to the problem were temporarily unavailable.
detail: We saw this only in the republished summary, not in KTEN's full text, which was cut short when we read it.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: The republished summary states both points and attributes them to KTEN.

claim_text: Some customers say money left their balance for orders that never went through
summary: Anonymous tracker comments say funds were taken from app balances for orders the store never received.
detail: These are unsigned comments on the tracker with no receipts. Starbucks has not confirmed any double charges.
label: Unverified
why_it_supports: The tracker shows three comments describing failed orders after a charge; they are unverified user accounts.

claim_text: Starbucks has not said what caused the problem
summary: No source we found names a cause. Starbucks said only that there was an issue.
detail: Starbucks said only that there was 'an issue'. Nothing we found from the company, a regulator or an outside researcher gives a cause.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: KTEN reports only an unspecified 'issue' and IBTimes Australia says Starbucks had not explained what caused the problems.

claim_text: No source reports a cyberattack on Starbucks
summary: No outlet, official or group we found says Starbucks was attacked, and no one has claimed it.
detail: Absence of a report is not proof there was no attack. It means nothing public points to one yet.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: Neither news report mentions an attack, a claim of responsibility or any security finding.

claim_text: Officials said this week they found no evidence the recent outages were connected or caused by a hostile actor
summary: IBTimes Australia, citing ConsumerAffairs, says the Director of National Intelligence and the Secretary of State said officials found no evidence the recent outages were connected or caused by a hostile actor.
detail: The statement is about the wider week of outages and does not name Starbucks. We did not read the original. IBTimes also says there is no indication Starbucks' problems are linked to the others.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: IBTimes Australia attributes the statement to officials and ConsumerAffairs; it is one outlet's second-hand account.

claim_text: The tracker shows several smaller Starbucks spikes earlier in November
summary: Instatus lists 10 Starbucks outage spikes in the last 90 days, including seven in Nov 1 to 6, all far smaller than Nov 20 (the largest, Nov 1, peaked at 600 reports an hour).
detail: Whether any of them share a cause with Nov 20 is not known.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: The tracker's past-outages list shows the dates and peak rates.
